label: VERIFIED
extraction: Agent orchestration 5 levels with cross-model consensus. Level 1: Single agent with good practices (default, most tasks). Level 2: Subagents for side work flooding main context (low coordination cost). Level 3: Headless pipelines for batch work over many items (low, deterministic). Level 4: Parallel sessions in git worktrees for independent workstreams (medium, manual). Level 5: Agent teams for parallel exploration with cross-communication (high coordination cost). Cross-model consensus: running agents from different vendors against same problem and comparing outputs - sits outside single-vendor levels. Token costs scale linearly with agents; coordination failures scale worse than linearly. Rule: move up a level only when current one demonstrably fails, never because parallelism sounds faster. Level 2 failure: parallel orchestrator coordinating dozen workers collapsed in production (session limits, lost state, workers dying silently). Strongest conclusion: orchestration is a question of coordination cost rather than framework choice.
